title: The Storage Impact of AI: How IT Leaders Are Handling AI Data Growth
summary: New research explores how AI data growth, egress fees, and provider lock-in are shaping IT leaders’ next cloud storage decisions.
body_markdown:
[Last year](https://www.backblaze.com/blog/the-hidden-cost-of-cloud-storage-what-400-it-leaders-wish-they-knew-sooner/) , research Backblaze commissioned from Dimensional Research found that 95% of IT decision-makers had been hit with unexpected cloud storage charges.[This year’s survey](https://www.backblaze.com/cloud-storage/landing/ad/the-storage-impact-of-ai) looked at what’s driving storage decisions now, and the answer is AI. Of the 407 cloud storage decision-makers surveyed, 84% say AI tooling and workflows have increased their data growth.


Most of those teams know their approach has to change. Among companies whose data is growing because of AI, 87% have changed or expect to change how they manage data, including continuity and disaster recovery. But only 34% have made that change so far. The other 53% expect to but haven’t started.


#### Download the Report


In this research from Dimensional Research, sponsored by Backblaze, IT decision makers share how AI is changing their storage needs.


[Send Me the Report](https://www.backblaze.com/cloud-storage/landing/ad/the-storage-impact-of-ai)


## The growth: AI is adding data almost everywhere


AI is now part of how most of these organizations use cloud storage. AI and machine learning is the second most common application running on cloud storage among respondents (55%), behind only BI and analytics (60%). And only 4% say they haven’t adopted AI tooling or workflows at all.


The effect on data volume is broad. Of all respondents, 84% say AI has increased their data growth, and 45% say the increase has been significant or dramatic.


## Where the data is going


When AI grows their data, most teams start with what they already have. Among companies whose data growth is driven by AI:


- 71% are increasing existing cloud storage
- 46% are adopting different storage tiers with their existing cloud providers
- 34% are increasing on-prem storage
- 32% are adding or switching cloud storage providers


Expanding existing storage is the easiest move, because it doesn’t require moving data or changing tools. But nearly a third of these teams are bringing in a new provider, which often means data moving between providers.


That movement has a cost. The largest providers have[waived egress fees since 2024](https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/688b8169fc784fa12a089071/Appendix_N_-_Egress_fees___free_switching_programmes.pdf) , but generally only for customers who leave completely. Teams that keep data with one provider and send it to another, for GPU compute or a backup copy, still pay every time it moves. For teams using more than one provider, egress is an ongoing cost, not a one-time exit fee.


## The gap: Most teams know they need to change, but haven’t yet


The clearest finding in the survey is the gap between knowing and doing. Among companies whose data is growing because of AI:


- 34% have already changed their approach to data management
- 53% haven’t changed yet, but expect they’ll have to
- 13% say their approach won’t change


Meanwhile, the data keeps growing while teams wait. The longer a team relies on its current setup, the more that choice can cost:


- Spend. Last year, 40% of those hit with surprise charges said they cut spending elsewhere in the tech stack to cover them, and AI growth adds volume to those same bills.
- Egress exposure. Egress is billed per gigabyte, so every terabyte that lands with the current provider raises the cost of moving or copying it later.
- Continuity. Every month a team waits to change how it manages AI data, there’s more data its continuity and disaster recovery plans have to cover.


Staying put is still a decision, even if it never shows up on anyone’s roadmap.


## The stack: Data has to follow compute


Where AI teams run their workloads is changing, too. Many are turning to specialized GPU clouds for compute, which means their GPUs and their data often end up with different providers. AI teams send data to whichever compute environment makes sense at the moment, and that can change month to month. The storage holding their data has to work with whichever provider runs the next job, without egress fees adding up every time the data moves.


Backblaze B2 Cloud Storage was built for that kind of setup. It’s S3-compatible, integrates with the GPU clouds and tools teams already use, and doesn’t make teams choose between where their data lives and where their compute runs. Egress to select GPU cloud partners is free and unlimited, so data can follow compute without a new bill every time it moves.


## The next step: What to do about it


If your data is growing because of AI and you haven’t changed how you manage it yet, you’re in the majority. A few places to start:


**Do the math.** Calculating what it would cost to move or copy your largest datasets, before the next contract renewal, gives you a number to negotiate with, and shows how fast that number grows as AI adds data.


**Start small.** A full migration doesn’t have to come first. A team can start by storing new data, or running a single new AI project, with a second provider. That shows whether the provider is fast enough and works with the team’s existing tools, without paying to move any data the team already has.


**Check where you stand.** Before your next renewal, ask:


- Have your continuity and disaster recovery plans kept pace with your AI data growth?
- If you had to move or copy your largest dataset next quarter, do you know what it would cost?
- Does your contract charge you every time data moves to another provider, or only waive fees if you leave entirely?
- If your next AI project runs on a GPU cloud, can your data get there without an egress bill?
